# Revised sections only — all other sections of the approved design are unchanged (design-only; no results claimed or implied)

## Rev. 1 — Kernel-path toggle folded into the matrix arithmetic

**§4 Decode (revised sentence):** All decode cells use the **fused** quantization-GEMM path by default. The **unfused** path is restricted to a budgeted subset: **C1 only, on 7B, batch {32, 64} × context {512, 4096} = 4 added cells.** What is lost by this restriction, stated explicitly: (a) the fused-vs-unfused delta for C4-analogous or C2/C3 paths is unmeasured — but those configs either don't use the QuaRot fused kernel (C4) or are ablations where the path-interaction question is secondary (C2/C3); (b) the unfused crossover batch is localized only to the ±1 grid step around the fused crossover (batches 32–64), not resolved across the full batch sweep. If the fused decode shows no regression anywhere in the sweep, item (b) loss is immaterial; if it regresses, the unfused subset is the diagnostic, which is why batch {32, 64} was chosen.

**§4 Prefill (revised, new sentence):** The fused/unfused distinction is **declared out of scope for prefill**. Rationale: prefill runs whole-matrix activation quantization that is already compute-dominated, and the fusion question is specific to the per-step decode kernel; the crossover sweep itself (batch {1,8}) is path-agnostic evidence. Concession noted in Limitations: any prefill regression attributable specifically to kernel fusion structure would not be separable from general 4-bit GEMM slowness.

**§7 Decode counts restated explicitly:**
- 7B decode primary: configs(3) × batch(4) × context(2) × {fused only} = **24**, **plus 4 unfused-subset cells (C1, batch {32,64} × context {512,4096}) = 28**.
- 7B decode optional (C2): 8 cells, fused path only.
- 13B decode: **6**, fused only; unfused out of scope for 13B.
- 70B decode: 2, fused only.
- Prefill counts unchanged (no path multiplier).

**§7 revised totals:** 7B primary = 30 prefill + 28 decode + 2 (C3 spot-check) = **60**, plus 9 harness-parity cells (Rev. 2) = **69**; optional 18. 13B = 15; 70B = 6; quality primary 28 (+10 optional). **New grand total ≈ 118 primary cells + 28 optional** (was ~105), plus the same ~168 microbenchmark runs and ~15 overhead measurement points. Rough GPU-hour budget increases by ~5–10 A100-hours → ≈ 85–150 hours for 7B/13B + ~20–40 for 70B `[A]`, unchanged in character.

## Rev. 2 — Harness-parity control as first-class cells (§7 additions; §10 uncertainty retained but now backed by cells)

**Primary denominator for speedup curves:** C1/C2/C3 speedups are divided by **BF16 on the QuaRot repo's unquantized path** (same harness as the treatments, isolating quantization rather than harness differences). C4 (GPTQ) ratios use BF16 on the HF harness (its native comparison harness); C4 ratios are therefore always reported harness-labeled and are never mixed into the C1 crossover curves.

**Added cells (7B, C0 on both harnesses, small parity grid):** prefill seq {512, 2048, 4096} × batch {1, 8} = 6, plus decode batch {1, 32, 64} × context {512} = 3 → 9 cells per harness. The HF side (9 runs) is already inside the existing C0 primary cells, so the **added count is +9** (QuaRot-harness C0), included in the §7 totals above.

**Decision rule (stated in the design, applied at analysis time):** if, at any parity cell, the two BF16 harness medians disagree by more than max(3% `[A]`, 2× within-cell repeat spread), then **all 7B speedup curves are reported as ratios against both BF16 harnesses** — no picking one after seeing treatment results; the rule is fixed pre-run and the classification of each parity cell is reported. If all cells agree within threshold, the single QuaRot-harness denominator is used and the parity check is reported as passing.

## Rev. 3 — New §7b: Attribution decision table (pattern → licensed claim wording)

All speed claims below are relative to the §7 Rev. 2 denominator and confined to the measured grids (batch ≤ 8 prefill, ≤ 64 decode; seq ≤ 4096); no extrapolation beyond the grid is licensed in any row. Quality classifications use the §5 noise-floor rule.

| Observed pattern | Licensed conclusion wording |
|---|---|
| C1−C0 quality within tolerance; decode speedup at batch 1; decode crossover at batch B* | "W4A4 improves decode throughput for batch ≤ B* on this hardware/kernel stack, with quality within the stated tolerance; beyond B* it is at parity or regresses (measured range)." |
| Prefill crossover lands below batch 8 (only batch-8 cells regress) | "W4A4 prefill wins at batch 1 (and short prompts) and regresses at batch 8 **within the measured grid**; the crossover lies in (1, 8) — location not resolved." Do not claim the regression extends beyond batch 8 or beyond 4096 tokens; a prefill regression is stated only if it exceeds 2× repeat spread (2×σ) at both batch-8 sequence points, else the prefill effect is classified as **not detected** and claimed as "within-noise across the measured grid." |
| C1−C3 quality delta significant, C1−C4 decode delta ≈ 0 (within noise) | "The quality benefit at W4A4 is attributable to the rotation (C3 collapses without it); the decode speed benefit is attributable to memory-footprint reduction, shared with weight-only W4 — activation quantization and the online Hadamard add quality capability at no measured decode-speed advantage." |
| C1−C3 quality delta within noise | "No measurable quality contribution from the rotation at W4A4 on this model set; W4A4 quality ≈ weight-only 4-bit quality." (This would be a surprising result and triggers the §8/source-verification check before being published, but the licensed wording is stated in advance.) |
| C1−C0 decode within noise at every batch | "No measurable decode benefit for W4A4 on this kernel stack" — claim permitted only after the §4 GEMM microbenchmarks classify it as kernel-bound vs method-bound; mechanism attribution stays conditional on the microbenchmarks. |
| C1−C0 prefill regresses at batch 1 (both short and long seq, beyond 2×σ) | "4-bit GEMMs are slower for large-M compute-bound shapes on this stack; QuaRot's value is confined to the decode regime (measured)." |
| Conflict rule: speed benefit exists but C1−C0 quality classified *degraded* (beyond acceptance gates) | Only the conditional wording is licensed: "the speed benefit is available at the cost of quality beyond the stated tolerance and is not claimable as an acceptable serving configuration under the §5 gates." Never "acceptable." |
| C1−C0 quality *degraded* and decode within noise | "No benefit observed and measurable quality cost" — a negative result stated directly; no softening language. |
| Multiple cells of the same config conflict with 13B trend | 7B-only claim wording with the model qualifier "for LLaMA-2-7B"; the 13B disagreement is reported, not averaged away. |

## Confirmation line (13B/70B independence from batch-8 prefill reclassification)

Confirmed: the 13B prefill grid is batch {1} only and the 70B prefill cells are batch {1} only, so neither model depends on the batch-8 prefill points, and the load-bearing/optional split in §7 is unchanged by Rev. 1.

**2. High-level approach skeleton**

*a) Models.* LLaMA-2 7B, 13B, 70B (HF checkpoints; LLaMA-2's published QuaRot results cover these). 7B primary for full sweep; 13B for trend confirmation; 70B for one representative config per phase to test scaling of the effect (70B W4A4 is what actually fits a single 80GB GPU in 4-bit).

*b) Quantization configurations.*
- BF16 baseline (HuggingFace / non-quantized reference).
- QuaRot full W4A4 end-to-end (all linear layers 4-bit weights + 4-bit activations, Hadamard rotations: online Hadamard on activations, fused Hadamard into weights, including the down-proj online Hadamard trick).
- Ablations isolating QuaRot components: (i) W4A16 (weight-only 4-bit, same rotation) — separates weight-quant vs activation-quant cost/benefit; (ii) Hadamard-averaging vs Hadamard-multiplication for the V/O-proj + residual handling (paper's "Ave" vs "Mul/Hadamard" variant — the paper recommends Ave for speed; measure both); (iii) skip-rotation W4A4 (RTN-style) to attribute quality deltas to the rotation vs to bit-width alone.
- Optional context: a strong baseline competitor (e.g., SmoothQuant/OmniQuant W8A8 or weight-only GPTQ W4) only if researcher wants external comparison; otherwise keep scope to QuaRot vs BF16.

*c) Phase separation (the core of the question).*
- **Prefill**: single forward pass on prompt-only inputs, measured via CUDA-event timing, excluding model load and quantization/rotation application (those are reported separately as one-time offline/one-time-online costs: rotation-fusion time, weight-quant time, calibration time). Sweep prompt lengths {128, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} at batch size 1 and a few batch-8 points (prefill is compute-bound; 4-bit GEMM speedup depends on whether the CUTLASS kernels give compute or only memory-bound gains).
- **Decode**: step-wise generation, measuring time-per-output-token (TPOT) and tokens/s with fused-quantization fused-GEMM kernel path, output lengths {32, 128, 512}, batch sizes {1, 8, 32, 64} (decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; this is where W4A4 should shine). Use a fixed prompt+generate harness (e.g., model.generate with static prompt batches) and measure steady-state (discard warmup tokens).
- Report prefill throughput (tokens/s processed) and decode throughput (tokens/s generated) separately; never a blended e2e number alone.

*d) Quality metrics.* Perplexity on WikiText2 (seq len 2048, standard non-overlapping evaluation) and C4; zero-shot accuracy (AI2 Benchmark lm-eval suite: PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC-e, WinoGrande, LAMBADA); optionally LongBench/AIME-free subset to show 4K-context behavior.
